newsitem.title: FRANCE: Vote to follow Jospin speech to French parliament.
newsitem.headline: Vote to follow Jospin speech to French parliament.

text.p: A major address to parliament next week by Socialist French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin will be followed, after all, by a confidence vote in the National Assembly, the new government said on Friday.

Assembly speaker Laurent Fabius, reading a note from Parliamentary Relations Minister Daniel Vaillant, had announced a day earlier that Jospin's speech, scheduled for next Thursday would not be followed by a vote of confidence in the new government.
Jospin and his cabinet have already begun work on the traditional statement, intended to inform parliament how he intends to translate his election promises into policy.

The speech is expected to include deadlines for carrying out key elements of his programme -- a revised budget and a national conference on jobs, wages and working hours uniting government, employers and trade unions.

The speech will be Jospin's first major policy address since the June 1 election which swept a leftist alliance including Socialists, Communists and Greens into power and ended four years of centre-right rule.
